title: Hacker Runs Hermes AI Agent Unattended for Post-Exploitation at Thai Finance Ministry

reading.body:
An autonomous AI agent called Hermes was deployed by attackers against Thailand's Ministry of Finance between July 9 and 13, 2026, running without human oversight in what was configured as "YOLO mode." This mode bypassed safety prompts that would normally prevent the agent from executing dangerous commands. The agent was left to operate unattended while the attacker staged a custom implant called Hades and prepared exploit code targeting the ministry's infrastructure, including Hadoop systems, mail services, and application servers.

The failure was deployment of an AI agent in a mode designed to remove safety constraints, enabling it to execute commands without review. A human operator configured this system knowing its safeguards would be disabled. The attack succeeded in gaining access to ministry networks and recovering session credentials; it is not established whether sensitive files were successfully stolen, though the operator attempted to enumerate and access personnel records.

What is not established: whether the attacker's intent was espionage, the full extent of data compromise, or whether the operator was state-sponsored, though the configuration contained Chinese text and the targeting of a government ministry's infrastructure suggests this possibility.

summary:
# Summary

Attackers targeted Thailand's Ministry of Finance using an autonomous AI agent called Hermes that operated without human oversight. Between July 9 and 13, 2026, researchers discovered three exposed directories on a Hong Kong server containing 585 files totaling 470 megabytes of attack code and stolen credentials. The operator deployed a custom implant called Hades across multiple systems and used specialized scripts to target the ministry's Hadoop infrastructure, mail systems, and GlassFish application servers. Session cookies and credentials recovered from the server indicate the attackers gained access to multiple ministry networks.

The attack was directed by a Chinese-speaking operator who configured the Hermes agent in "YOLO mode," which bypassed safety prompts for dangerous commands. The operator accessed the staging server from a fourth Hong Kong IP address and left traces including the Chinese word for "Thunder God" in the agent's configuration. Thailand's Ministry of Finance and national cybersecurity authorities were notified on July 15, 2026. Researchers identified privilege escalation exploits ready for deployment and evidence the operator attempted to enumerate and access sensitive personnel records, though successful file theft was not confirmed.
